Walking direction in the lab for the Left side segmented strides (in order as appears in the data matrix)

These events (and related data) are given for both the left side segmented strides ("L_") and the right side segmented strides ("R_"). Segmentation is based on both the available foot marker data (either left or right side) and force plate data if good data was available.

1 = good landing on the forceplate, data useful for kinetic analysis.
0 = no good landing on the force plate, data useful for (isolated) kinematic analysis.
Select the subject number (#) of interest
This file describes the MAT-files with time-normalized gait data of able-bodied participants and post-stroke participants.
This file is part of paper X

Initial contact of the contra-lateral leg that falls within the stride of interest 
this is the index number, within the trial of the initial contact of the contra-lateral leg, that falls within the stride of interest. NaN if not available, events taken from Vicon Nexus, visually checked and corrected if needed.

Initial contact of the ipsilateral leg: heel landing that formed start of a complete stride.
Taken from the C3D files (automatically detected with the software Vicon Nexus) and checked in Matlab. For strides with good force data, initial contact was determined again based on a threshold of 0.5 n/kg, and corrected if the old events deviated. Initial contacts were checked against foot marker data and force plate data -if available - and corrected manually if needed. This contains the absolute index values of the respective trial the stride was taken from.

Initial contact of the ipsilateral leg: heel landing that formed the end of a complete stride. 
See description ICstart

Toe-off event of the ipsilateral leg that falls within the stride of interest
This is is the absolute index number that falls within the stride of interest in the respective trial. NaN if not available. Events are taken from Vicon Nexus, visuall checked and corrected if needed.
Relative timing (1-1001) within the stride of interest of TO.
Relative timing (1-1001) within the stride of interest of IC_cnt.

Toe-off event of the contralateral leg that falls within the stride of interest
This is the absolute index number, within the trial of the toe-off of the contra-lateral leg, that falls within the stride of interest. NaN if not available. Events are taken from Vicon Nexus, visuall checked and corrected if needed.
Relative timing (1-1001) within the stride of interest of TO_cnt.
This section contains all the kinematic and kinetic data for specific sides of the body
This section contains all the kinematic and kinetic data for the general body (B)

This section contains all the kinematic, kinetic and EMG data.
This data is stride-normalized (0-1000 samples) based on the events (see above) and contains as many strides as were available for that individual. When no data was available (EMG) or there was no good landing on the force plate (no kinetic data), the stride is filled with NaN (1x1001). Some variables were checked and outliers set tot NaN as well. 
- data is either segmented for the left side (Lsegmented) or right side(Rsegmented) for the able-bodied and paretic side (Psegmented) non-paretic side (Nsegmented). Which side is the paretic side, can be found in the sub_char field.
- Data that are available for either the left or right side of the body (eg ankle angle) are given for both the side left side of the body (_Ldata), right side of the body (_Rdata). Other data (eg center of mass) is given in Bdata. 
- Each variable has its dimensions (eg x,y,z for markers or n for uni-dimensional data such as power and EMG) 
- Data structure for a certain variable: 
          LsideSegm_BsideData.C7.x [1001x7]
         For this participant there are 7 time-normalized strides available.
         We are looking at the C7 neck marker in the x dimension, that are from Left-side initial contact to next left side initial contact.
Marker, data in mm, dimensions: x (anterior-posterior), y (medio-lateral), z (vertical)
Position of the center of mass in mm, dimensions: x (anterior-posterior), y (medio-lateral), z (vertical)

Ground reaction moment in Nm normalized to body weight, dimensions: x (sagittal),y,z

Joint power in W normalized to body weight, dimensions: n
Joint force in N normalized to body weight, dimensions: x (sagittal),y,z

% READ-IN AND PLOT TIME-NORMALIZED DATA STRUCTURES
% Example code to use the structure.
%
%
% input: time-normalized structure van Criekinge et al, 2022
% eg. MAT_normalizedData_AbleBodiedAdults_v06-03-23
% eg. MAT_normalizedData_PostStrokeAdults_v27-02-23
%
% output: 
% Figure of the selected variable of interest (.fig and .png)
%
% 
% 19.09.2023, Lizeth Sloot, Heidelberg University / Newcastle University.
%
%
% MIT License:
% 
% Copyright (c) 2022 Lizeth Sloot (LizSloot)
%

% to use, copy, modify, merge, publish, distribute, sublicense, and/or sell
% copies of the Software, and to permit persons to whom the Software is
% furnished to do so, subject to the following conditions:
% 
% The above copyright notice and this permission notice shall be included in all
% copies or substantial portions of the Software.
% 
% THE SOFTWARE IS PROVIDED "AS IS", WITHOUT WARRANTY OF ANY KIND, EXPRESS OR
% IMPLIED, INCLUDING BUT NOT LIMITED TO THE WARRANTIES OF MERCHANTABILITY,
% FITNESS FOR A PARTICULAR PURPOSE AND NONINFRINGEMENT. IN NO EVENT SHALL THE
% AUTHORS OR COPYRIGHT HOLDERS BE LIABLE FOR ANY CLAIM, DAMAGES OR OTHER
% LIABILITY, WHETHER IN AN ACTION OF CONTRACT, TORT OR OTHERWISE, ARISING FROM,
% OUT OF OR IN CONNECTION WITH THE SOFTWARE OR THE USE OR OTHER DEALINGS IN THE
% SOFTWARE.

close all
clear all
clc


%% General Settings

%%% 1. Set path to directory of the Structure you want to load!
settings.mainDir = pwd;


%%% 2. Load Structure
% Give the name of the structure you want to load:
settings.StructName = 'MAT_normalizedData_PostStrokeAdults_v27-02-23';
StructTime = load(fullfile(settings.mainDir,settings.StructName));


%%% 3. Set saving settings
settings.SaveFig = 1;       % set to 1 if you want to save the figure, set to 0 if not.
settings.SaveDir = fullfile(settings.mainDir,'Figures');


%%% 4. Set Figure settings
% Set the "Sides" as defined in the Structure. 
% (eg. DataStruct.Sub(1).PsideSegm_PsideData --> PsideSegm and NPsideSegm)
% For Able bodied (MAT_normalizedData_AbleBodiedAdults_v06-03-23), this is
% left and right (or SideA = {'LR';'LR'})
% For Stroke (MAT_normalizedData_PostStrokeAdults_v27-02-23), this is
% paretic and non-paretic side (or SideA = {'PN';'PN'};)
% SideA = {'LR';'LR'}; 
settings.SideA = {'PN';'PN'};

% Both sides are plotted in a different color and line type. 
% note, first side (defined above) will get the first color.
settings.ColorZ = 'br';
settings.MarkerSymbol = {'-';'--'};

% Set the number of subplots in a single figure. 
% if you set it lower, the subplot per participant will get larger, but
% less will fit in a single figure. 
% For Able bodied, 12x12 seems to work well. 
% For Stroke, 7x8 seems to work well. 
settings.iCol = 7;        
settings.iRow = 8;    



%% Select the data you want to plot

%%% 1. Specify the variable(s) of interest to plot:
% You can give a series of variables (it will run in a loop) or a single
% one.
varsInt = {'AnkleAngles';'CentreOfMass'};
    

%%% 2. Specify the dimension to plot for each of these variables:
% This can be x, y, z, or n (non-dimensional). Check the Structure.
DimsC={'x','x'};    


%%% 3. Specify the body side of the data you want to look at
% The code will plot both the e.g. Left-side-segmented (stride normalized
% based on left side gait events) and the Right-side-segmented data. 
% Here you specify if you want to plot the left ankle angle from the
% left-side segmented data (ipsilateral side), or the right ankle angle
% (contra-lateral side). Usually, this will be the same as in settings.SideA.
% (eg. DataStruct.Sub(1).PsideSegm_PsideData --> PsideData and NPsideData)
% If you are interested in whole-body parameters that aren't related to one
% side (eg center-of-mass, sternum marker), use 'BB').
SideS= {'PN';'BB'};


  
%% DO NOT CHANGE ANYTHING AFTER THIS SECTION

iDim=length(DimsC);

% Get Screen size
scrsz = get(0,'ScreenSize');
scrplt.x(1) = round( scrsz(3)*0.05 );
scrplt.x(2) = round( scrsz(3)*0.75 );
scrplt.y(1) = round( scrsz(4)*0.05 );
scrplt.y(2) = round( scrsz(4)*0.75 );

% Graph per var:
for iVar = 1%:length(varsInt)
    disp(['Working on plotting var: ',varsInt{iVar}])
    
    % Average data
    TelSub.L = 1; TelSub.R = 1; TelSub.B = 1; TelSub.P = 1; TelSub.N = 1; 
    clear Temp Hfig SidesLeg
    for iSub = 1:size(StructTime.Sub,2)  
        for iSide = 1:length(settings.SideA)
            if ~isempty( StructTime.Sub(iSub). ...
                    ([settings.SideA{iSide}(iSide),'sideSegm_',SideS{iVar}(iSide),'sideData']) )
                if isfield(StructTime.Sub(iSub). ...
                        ([settings.SideA{iSide}(iSide),'sideSegm_',SideS{iVar}(iSide),'sideData']),...
                        ([varsInt{iVar}]))
                    if isfield(StructTime.Sub(iSub). ...
                            ([settings.SideA{iSide}(iSide),'sideSegm_',SideS{iVar}(iSide),'sideData']).([varsInt{iVar}]),...
                            (DimsC{iVar}))
                        
                        Temp.(settings.SideA{iSide}(iSide))(TelSub.(SideS{iSide}(iSide)),:) = ...
                            nanmean(StructTime.Sub(iSub). ...
                            ([settings.SideA{iSide}(iSide),'sideSegm_',SideS{iVar}(iSide),'sideData']). ...
                            ([varsInt{iVar}]).(DimsC{iVar}),2);
                        
                        TelSub.(SideS{iSide}(iSide))=TelSub.(SideS{iSide}(iSide))+1;
                    end
                end
            end
        end % iSide
    end % iSub
    
    % Initiate figure
    figure, set(gcf,'name',varsInt{iVar},'color',[1 1 1],'position',...
        [scrplt.x(1) scrplt.y(1) scrplt.x(2) scrplt.y(2)])    
    
    % Plot individual data
    tiledlayout(settings.iCol,settings.iRow, 'Padding', 'none', 'TileSpacing', 'compact'); 
    for iSub = 1:size(StructTime.Sub,2)
        nexttile 
        if length(SideS{iVar})>1
            Temp0 = [Temp.(settings.SideA{1}(1))(:,1:10:end); Temp.(settings.SideA{1}(1))(:,1:10:end)];
            
        else
            Temp0 = Temp.B(:,1:10:end);
        end
        xdata = 0:10:(size(Temp0,2)-1)*10;  
        if (min(nanmean(Temp0))<0 && max(nanmean(Temp0))>0)
            plot(xdata,zeros(length(xdata)),'-k'),
        end
        hold on, clear Temp0
        
        for iSide = 1:length(settings.SideA)
            if ~isempty( StructTime.Sub(iSub). ...
                    ([settings.SideA{iSide}(iSide),'sideSegm_',SideS{iVar}(iSide),'sideData']) )
                if isfield(StructTime.Sub(iSub). ...
                        ([settings.SideA{iSide}(iSide),'sideSegm_',SideS{iVar}(iSide),'sideData']),...
                        ([varsInt{iVar}]))
                    if isfield(StructTime.Sub(iSub). ...
                            ([settings.SideA{iSide}(iSide),'sideSegm_',SideS{iVar}(iSide),'sideData']).([varsInt{iVar}]),...
                            (DimsC{iVar}))
                        
                        if iSub==1 % to create legend
                        Hfig(iSide) = plot(xdata, StructTime.Sub(iSub). ...
                            ([settings.SideA{iSide}(iSide),'sideSegm_',SideS{iVar}(iSide),'sideData']). ...
                            ([varsInt{iVar}]).(DimsC{iVar})(1:10:end,1),'color',settings.ColorZ(iSide),'linewidth',1.5);
                        end 
                        
                        plot(xdata, StructTime.Sub(iSub). ...
                            ([settings.SideA{iSide}(iSide),'sideSegm_',SideS{iVar}(iSide),'sideData']). ...
                            ([varsInt{iVar}]).(DimsC{iVar})(1:10:end,:),'color',settings.ColorZ(iSide),'linewidth',1.5);
                        
                        TelSub.(SideS{iVar}(iSide))=TelSub.(SideS{iVar}(iSide))+1;
                    end
                end
            end
        end % iSide        
        
        ylabel(['Subno:',num2str(iSub)])
    end
    
    
    % Create legend
    for iSide = 1:length(settings.SideA)
        SidesLeg{iSide} = SideS{iVar}(iSide);
    end
    legend(Hfig,SidesLeg)
    
    
    %%% Save
    if settings.SaveFig==1
        saveas(gcf,[settings.SaveDir,varsInt{iVar},'_',DimsC{iVar}],'fig')
        saveas(gcf,[settings.SaveDir,varsInt{iVar},'_',DimsC{iVar}],'png')
        disp(['Figs ',varsInt{iVar},' saved.'])
    end
    
    
end % iVar



% EOF
